summary: Tested portfolio backend (7 pytest tests, all passed) and frontend e2e (Nav, Hero, About, Work, Contact). All 4 projects loaded from /api/projects and rendered as project rows. Contact form valid submission persisted to MongoDB and showed success. Invalid email is blocked by HTML5 native validation (no contact-error rendered).

integration_issues.issue: Email field uses HTML5 type='email' so browser blocks submit silently — the app-level [data-testid=contact-error] element never appears for invalid email. Spec says 'Contact form shows error for invalid email'. Either remove type='email' and rely on server 422 + setState({error}), or add client-side regex validation that sets state.error before submit.

action_items: Minor: Add client-side email validation in Contact.jsx so [data-testid=contact-error] is rendered for invalid email instead of relying solely on HTML5 native popup (or remove type='email' so submission reaches backend and shows server 422 message).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: ContactCreate uses EmailStr (good); empty name/message correctly rejected via min_length.
All Mongo reads use projection {_id: 0} — no _id leak verified.
PROJECTS list is in-memory (static seed) — fine for portfolio scope.
Consider adding rate-limiting / spam protection on POST /api/contact for production.
seed_data_creation: Inserted one TEST_ contact message via POST /api/contact during pytest.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py covers root, /projects, /projects/{id}, 404, /contact create+list+validation. Frontend testids all present: site-nav, nav-link-{work,about,contact}, hero-section, hero-title, about-section, skill-*, about-fact-*, work-section, project-row-{proj-orbit|proj-glass|proj-paper|proj-signal}, contact-form, contact-name, contact-email, contact-message, contact-submit, contact-success, contact-error. Only the invalid-email path leaves contact-error unrendered (HTML5 blocks submit).
rca of the issue: Contact.jsx email input has type='email'. When invalid value is entered, browser prevents form submit so the handler that would set state.error never runs. Fix: change to type='text' + add JS regex validation, OR keep type='email' but additionally validate in onSubmit and set state.error('Please enter a valid email').
